anchors.1: Does not address the bug. Broken code is returned unchanged, is syntactically invalid, or introduces an immediate NameError/ImportError.
anchors.2: Recognises the intent but is wrong or incomplete: raises an unexpected exception type, handles only the happy path, silently returns a wrong value, or ignores an explicit requirement in the instruction.
anchors.3: Fixes the stated bug and passes the visible tests, but misses a stated requirement or degrades an edge case (empty input, boundary value, non-mutation, wrong exception type).
anchors.4: Correct for all stated requirements and edge cases. Minor style or idiom deviations only; no behavioural difference from the reference.
anchors.5: Correct, complete, and robust beyond the stated requirements: handles inputs the tests never exercise, does not mutate caller state, and the code reads like idiomatic Python.

judge_family_rule: The judge must be a different model FAMILY from every model it grades. Both codefix-v1 subjects are Alibaba Qwen (groq) and Google Gemini (google), so the judge is OpenAI gpt-oss. Same-family judging shares blind spots and is not evidence of anything.
